content.text: {"questions":[{"id":"RQ-001","criterion_id":"design_intent","question":"Are the objectives (Section 1 scope and volume baseline), principles P1-P10, FR/NFR requirements and confirmed decisions (Section 24) stated precisely enough to review against? In particular, does FR-8's '2%' mean percentage points or a relative change, given that Sections 10.3 and 24 write 'default 2' with no unit?","rationale":"FR-8 sets the routing trade-off and is an approved decision, so the review cannot judge Section 10.3 or the FR-8 test until its unit is fixed.","needs_external":false,"capability":"none","queries":[],"section_refs":["1","2.1","3","10.3","24"]},{"id":"RQ-002","criterion_id":"fitness_for_objectives","question":"Can the DynamoDB idempotency table (partition key merchant_id, an LSI on created_at, response bodies up to 4 KB) hold the largest merchant's 900 TPS? Two DynamoDB limits matter here: the per-partition write ceiling, which Section 9.3 states as 10,000 WCU, and the 10 GB item-collection limit that applies to tables with an LSI. One merchant's 24 hours of records could reach tens of GB.","rationale":"FR-5, NFR-1 and the confirmed idempotency-store decision all rest on Section 9.3. If the claimed per-partition ceiling is wrong, the largest merchant gets throttled or writes fail at campaign peak.","needs_external":true,"capability":"none","queries":["DynamoDB partition throughput limit 1000 WCU per second","DynamoDB local secondary index item collection size limit 10 GB","DynamoDB write capacity unit item size 1 KB"],"section_refs":["9.2","9.3","24"]},{"id":"RQ-003","criterion_id":"security_and_privacy","question":"The Redis fast-path key is idem:resp:{idempotency_key}, with no merchant_id and no request-hash check. Does this break P3 and FR-5? Could it return one merchant's stored payment response to another merchant who reuses the same order-ID key, and does it skip the 422 that FR-5 requires for a reused key with a different body?","rationale":"The document itself says merchants often use order IDs as keys. Without merchant scoping, keys will collide across merchants, which leaks data and returns wrong responses, against P3 and FR-5.","needs_external":false,"capability":"none","queries":[],"section_refs":["3","9.1","9.2","24"]},{"id":"RQ-004","criterion_id":"claims_and_external_constraints","question":"Do PCI DSS v4.0 / v4.0.1 Requirements 3.2.1 and 3.3.2 actually allow a service provider to keep an encrypted CVC after authorization, until settlement or for up to 72 hours, for cascade re-presentation and incremental authorizations? Or does Requirement 3.3.1 forbid keeping SAD after authorization completes?","rationale":"NFR-6, Section 12.4 and the confirmed CVC-handling decision depend on this reading. If it is wrong, the platform cannot pass the Level 1 assessment required by NFR-5.","needs_external":true,"capability":"none","queries":["PCI DSS v4.0.1 requirement 3.3.1 sensitive authentication data not retained after authorization","PCI DSS 3.3.2 storage of SAD prior to completion of authorization","PCI DSS v4.0 retirement v4.0.1"],"section_refs":["2.2","12.4","24","26.2"]},{"id":"RQ-005","criterion_id":"security_and_privacy","question":"The Fraud Hook detokenises the PAN using the Card Adapter's service role and then sends the full card number to FRV-1. Does that contradict P2, P9, the Section 12.1 rule that only the Card Adapter may detokenise, and the Section 12.2 table that places the Fraud Hook out of CDE scope? And is FRV-1 tracked as a PCI third-party service provider and a cross-border personal-data processor, while its DPA is still pending in Backlog item 4?","rationale":"This decides whether the CDE scope in NFR-5 holds and whether card data reaches a vendor whose contract is not yet signed.","needs_external":false,"capability":"none","queries":[],"section_refs":["3","12.1","12.2","13.1","25"]},{"id":"RQ-006","criterion_id":"scalability_and_failure_modes","question":"Can NFR-4's zero RPO for authorized payments and ledger postings be met with Aurora Global Database, whose cross-region replication is asynchronous? After a regional failover, can idempotency state really be 'reconstructed from the payment table' when that table stores no idempotency key, and if not, do merchant retries cause duplicate charges?","rationale":"NFR-4 and FR-5 conflict with the confirmed DR decision. After a regional failover that could mean lost postings or double charges.","needs_external":true,"capability":"none","queries":["Aurora Global Database RPO asynchronous replication unplanned failover data loss","Aurora Global Database managed failover vs switchover RPO"],"section_refs":["2.2","19","20.2","24","26.2"]},{"id":"RQ-007","criterion_id":"scalability_and_failure_modes","question":"Is a single CloudHSM in ap-southeast-1a, restored from daily backups, compatible with 99.95% availability (NFR-3), and how long does restoring an HSM from backup take? If the HSM is down, the Vault returns 503, which the Card Adapter treats as retryable. Does that make every card payment cascade three times and then fail, piling extra load on the platform?","rationale":"Every card authorization needs detokenisation, so one HSM is a single point of failure for card acceptance and directly affects NFR-3. The approved decision is one HSM at launch.","needs_external":true,"capability":"none","queries":["AWS CloudHSM high availability recommendation multiple HSMs AZs","AWS CloudHSM create HSM from backup time","AWS CloudHSM single HSM cluster SLA"],"section_refs":["12.3","20.1","24","2.2"]},{"id":"RQ-008","criterion_id":"internal_consistency","question":"Section 21.1 says fewer than 1% of card payments cascade. Does that agree with the 3.8% retryable rate in Section 10.5 and the 3.8% injection in the NFR-2 test? With a 2,500 ms attempt timeout, can a cascade ever finish within NFR-2's 1,500 ms p99 bound, which explicitly includes cascades? Does the budget also leave out 3DS and the Fraud Hook's extra detokenise call?","rationale":"The NFR-2 latency claim and its acceptance test rest on a number that conflicts with another part of the document.","needs_external":false,"capability":"none","queries":[],"section_refs":["10.5","11.1","21.1","26.2"]},{"id":"RQ-009","criterion_id":"scalability_and_failure_modes","question":"A response that arrives after the 2,500 ms timeout is discarded, and the payment then cascades to another acquirer. What happens if that late response was an approval? The design has no reversal or void for orphaned approvals, so the customer may carry two authorization holds, and Section 11.2's claim that 'cascading cannot create a duplicate charge' would be wrong.","rationale":"FR-5, FR-7 and P1 all depend on having no duplicate authorizations. A known timeout-then-approve race at the acquirer is not handled.","needs_external":false,"capability":"none","queries":[],"section_refs":["11.1","11.2","20.3"]},{"id":"RQ-010","criterion_id":"claims_and_external_constraints","question":"What are the current Visa and Mastercard rules on reattempts and cascading, including whether a soft decline 05 sent to a second acquirer counts as a reattempt, the 30-day reattempt limits, and which response codes are Category 1 or 'do not reattempt'? Does Section 11's classification follow them?","rationale":"FR-7 promises never to breach scheme rules, yet Section 11.3 refers to 'scheme limits' without stating them, while Section 27 rates the Retry Engine as Ready.","needs_external":true,"capability":"none","queries":["Visa reattempt rules category 1 2 3 decline codes 15 reattempts 30 days","Mastercard excessive retry merchant advice code 03 21","cascading authorization different acquirer scheme rules"],"section_refs":["11.1","11.3","27"]},{"id":"RQ-011","criterion_id":"claims_and_external_constraints","question":"Do Indonesian rules (Bank Indonesia payment-system rules, QRIS, national payment gateway (GPN) domestic routing, GR 71/2019) or other markets' rules require domestic processing or domestic storage of transaction data? If so, how does that affect hosting in Singapore only and routing Indonesian domestic cards to the regional acquirer ACQ-SG2?","rationale":"NFR-7 and the confirmed region decision could conflict with data-localisation and domestic-routing obligations in the largest market (4,200 merchants).","needs_external":true,"capability":"none","queries":["Bank Indonesia regulation payment system data processing domestic location","Indonesia GPN domestic debit card routing requirement","Indonesia GR 71 2019 data localisation private electronic system operator"],"section_refs":["2.2","4","19.1","24"]},{"id":"RQ-012","criterion_id":"requirement_completeness","question":"Which control and error paths are missing? Candidates: MFA for the Finance role that can change payout bank accounts, with notification only to the person who made the change; refund failure and refund-state handling; partial-capture transitions; reconciliation exception ageing and ownership; a disputes interim process; and rollback of a failed payout.","rationale":"FR-13, FR-15 and FR-17 move money. An unprotected change to a payout bank account is a direct route to merchant funds being diverted.","needs_external":false,"capability":"none","queries":[],"section_refs":["7.2","16.3","18.2","18.3","18.4","25"]},{"id":"RQ-013","criterion_id":"fitness_for_objectives","question":"Can NFR-8 (reports by 08:00 SGT on T+1) be met when the matcher waits for every file? ACQ-TH1's file arrives at 06:30 ICT (07:30 SGT), and matching plus reporting already takes 60 minutes at 2025 volume, which roughly doubles by 2027. The design also has no rule for a late or missing file, such as ACQ-PH1's XLSX.","rationale":"Simple arithmetic on the document's own figures suggests NFR-8 is not achievable.","needs_external":false,"capability":"none","queries":[],"section_refs":["16.1","16.2","2.2","26.2"]},{"id":"RQ-014","criterion_id":"assumptions_and_dependencies","question":"Which decisions marked confirmed or Ready depend on unresolved items? Examples: network tokens as the primary credential 'from launch' while the TRID application has not been submitted (Backlog 2, Build Phase 3 'No - ready'); FRV-1 while its contract is pending; reconciliation parsers that still lack sample files; and the scheme reattempt limits.","rationale":"Stating readiness when it depends on pending items puts FR-14, FR-9 and the build plan at risk.","needs_external":false,"capability":"none","queries":[],"section_refs":["12.5","24","25","27","28"]},{"id":"RQ-015","criterion_id":"verifiability","question":"Can each acceptance criterion actually prove its requirement? For example: the FR-5 test is sequential only, with no concurrent duplicates; the NFR-4 game day can pass when lag happens to be zero; NFR-3 needs a definition of availability; NFR-6 needs a defined test; NFR-9 is tested at 3× the rate limit, but the largest merchant alone is 45% of load; and NFR-7 has no test of retention or erasure.","rationale":"Without valid tests, the build cannot show that the core FR and NFR obligations are met before go-live.","needs_external":false,"capability":"none","queries":[],"section_refs":["26.1","26.2","2.2"]},{"id":"RQ-016","criterion_id":"decision_preservation","question":"Which confirmed decisions (CVC handling, one HSM, Aurora Global DR, the idempotency store's key schema, network tokens from launch) can be refined while preserved? Is there enough evidence (two or more items) to challenge any of them, particularly CVC handling and the asynchronous DR approach against NFR-4 and NFR-6?","rationale":"Findings against approved decisions need the relation (preserves, refines or challenges) to be explicit and backed by evidence.","needs_external":false,"capability":"none","queries":[],"section_refs":["24","12.3","12.4","20.2","9.2"]},{"id":"RQ-017","criterion_id":"operability_and_governance","question":"Does the build sequence (Fraud Hook in Phase 8, then hardening, PCI assessment and DR game day in Phase 9, all after first-cohort go-live at the end of Phase 7) mean launching without FR-9 and without a PCI Report on Compliance (NFR-5)? Are owners named for routing weights, fraud thresholds, reconciliation exceptions, risk acceptance and runbooks?","rationale":"Going live before compliance and fraud controls exist is a governance decision that needs an accountable owner.","needs_external":false,"capability":"none","queries":[],"section_refs":["10.3","13.2","16.2","27","28"]},{"id":"RQ-018","criterion_id":"internal_consistency","question":"Which elements are sound and consistent with the principles? Candidates: integer money (P4), same-transaction ledger plus outbox (P5, P7), the asynchronous balance projector, webhook signing and SSRF controls, back-office JIT elevation, and the arithmetic of the ledger examples and the webhook retry schedule.","rationale":"Affirming elements that are fit for purpose keeps the review balanced and steers it away from redesign.","needs_external":false,"capability":"none","queries":[],"section_refs":["14","15","17","18.5","21.2"]}],"criteria_skipped":[]}

{"intent_summary":{"statement":"MPOP is Serindit Pay's Merchant Payment Orchestration Platform. It accepts payment requests from merchants, routes each one to an acquirer, e-wallet provider or bank-transfer rail, and accounts for every resulting movement of money until it is settled to the merchant. It replaces five per-market integration stacks with one merchant API across Singapore, Malaysia, Indonesia, Thailand and the Philippines. It provides routing with cascading, idempotency, a tokenising card vault that limits PCI DSS scope, a fraud-scoring hook, a double-entry ledger, daily reconciliation, payouts, signed webhooks and a merchant admin plane. The 2027 target is about 15,000 merchants at a peak of 2,000 TPS. Disputes case management, KYB, 3DS server internals and lending/BNPL are out of scope.","objectives":[{"ref":null,"text":"Replace five per-market integration stacks, which share no routing or ledger and reconcile by spreadsheet, with one governed platform."},{"ref":null,"text":"Provide one versioned merchant API across five markets for about 15,000 active merchants at a peak of 2,000 payment-creation TPS (2027 target)."},{"ref":"P1","text":"One payment, one truth: the payment record and the ledger are the source of truth; provider responses are only inputs."},{"ref":"P2","text":"Card data stays in the Vault: PAN and SAD never leave the Vault boundary except over the Card Adapter's connection to an acquirer; all other services handle tokens only."},{"ref":"P3","text":"Idempotency is scoped to the pair (merchant, key) for every mutating call."},{"ref":"P4","text":"Money is integers: amounts are integer minor units with an ISO 4217 code, and no floating-point type ever holds an amount."},{"ref":"P5","text":"The ledger is append-only; corrections are new reversing or adjusting journals."},{"ref":"P6","text":"Adapters absorb provider differences; the core never branches on provider identity."},{"ref":"P7","text":"At-least-once delivery with exactly-once effect through consumer deduplication on stable identifiers."},{"ref":"P8","text":"Fail closed on security failures; degrade gracefully to documented defaults when optional enrichment fails."},{"ref":"P9","text":"Least privilege and separation of duties; money-moving permissions are separated from configuration permissions."},{"ref":"P10","text":"Everything is auditable: every mutation, routing decision and admin action can be reconstructed."},{"ref":"NFR-10","text":"New acquirers or providers are onboarded through the Connector interface plus configuration only."}],"constraints":[{"ref":"NFR-5","text":"The platform must be assessed as a PCI DSS v4.0 Level 1 service provider, with the CDE limited to the components listed in Section 12.2."},{"ref":"NFR-6","text":"Sensitive authentication data must be handled per PCI DSS v4.0 Req. 3.2.1/3.3.2: encrypted, held only in the Vault, and deleted at settlement."},{"ref":"NFR-7","text":"Personal data must comply with SG PDPA 2012, MY PDPA 2010, ID Law 27/2022, TH PDPA 2019 and PH DPA 2012."},{"ref":"FR-7","text":"Card reattempts must never occur where card scheme rules prohibit them."},{"ref":null,"text":"All workloads and primary data stores run in AWS ap-southeast-1 across three AZs; ap-southeast-3 is used only for disaster recovery."},{"ref":null,"text":"Principles win over later sections where the two conflict (Section 3)."},{"ref":null,"text":"Merchant onboarding/KYB is handled by the Merchant Risk platform; MPOP consumes an approved-merchant event."},{"ref":null,"text":"Payment and attempt records are retained 7 years, audit records 5 years, and idempotency records 24 hours."},{"ref":null,"text":"ACQ-PH1 v2 API retires in Q3 2027, so the adapter must migrate before then."},{"ref":null,"text":"The first cohort (Singapore, cards and PayNow) goes live after Phase 7; other markets follow at four-week intervals."}],"key_assumptions":[{"ref":null,"text":"Volume grows from 1,140 to 2,000 peak TPS and from 9,800 to 15,000 merchants by 2027; the largest merchant reaches a 45% share of peak."},{"ref":null,"text":"Fewer than 1% of card payments cascade, so cascades sit above p99 and do not affect the latency budget."},{"ref":null,"text":"A single DynamoDB partition sustains up to 10,000 WCU/s, enough for the largest merchant at about 1,800 WCU."},{"ref":null,"text":"PCI DSS v4.0 Req. 3.2.1/3.3.2 permit encrypted CVC retention until settlement (max 72 hours) for cascades and incremental authorizations."},{"ref":null,"text":"One CloudHSM with daily backups is adequate until sustained card volume exceeds 1,500 TPS."},{"ref":null,"text":"FRV-1 scoring quality needs the full PAN, which the Fraud Hook obtains through Vault detokenise."},{"ref":null,"text":"Aurora Global Database asynchronous replication with typical lag under 1 s supports the DR objectives."},{"ref":null,"text":"A spike test of 2,600 TPS on db.r7g.8xlarge supports sizing the writer at db.r7g.12xlarge."},{"ref":null,"text":"ACQ-SG2 is licensed in all five markets and serves as the default cascade secondary."},{"ref":null,"text":"Cascading recovers about 31% of retryable outcomes, based on a three-month ACQ-SG1 to ACQ-SG2 pilot."},{"ref":null,"text":"The first cohort can operate with disputes handled manually by Finance Operations and with the portal instead of the Admin API."},{"ref":null,"text":"Network tokens are
